target.title: fix(doctor): stream heartbeat transcript scans without full-file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor heartbeat main-session repair loaded the entire session transcript with `fs.readFileSync` before deciding whether the main session was heartbeat-poisoned. A large JSONL transcript (common after long heartbeat-only ownership) forced the whole file into one string during `openclaw doctor` state integrity. Chunked reads alone were also insufficient if a single JSONL record (or a missing newline) kept growing the carry buffer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scan the transcript with a fixed-size sync chunk reader (`openSync` + `readSync` + `StringDecoder`) and cap retained JSONL records at 256 KiB. Oversized incomplete or complete records fail closed (no heartbeat classification / no repair) so memory stays bounded even for malformed transcripts. Keep the call sites synchronous because `resolveHeartbeatMainSessionRepairCandidate` runs inside the session-store update path.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor --fix` can classify and move heartbeat-owned main sessions even when the transcript is multi-megabyte, without risking an OOM from a single full-file string read or an unbounded carry buffer. Mixed transcripts and oversized single records still block repair.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

#### Behavior or issue addressed

Large heartbeat-only transcripts are scanned in chunks; doctor still moves the poisoned main session; a single oversized JSONL record declines repair; the transcript path is never loaded via `readFileSync`.

#### Canonical reachability path

`openclaw doctor --fix --yes` → `noteStateIntegrity` → `repairHeartbeatPoisonedMainSession` → `resolveHeartbeatMainSessionRepairCandidate` → `summarizeTranscriptHeartbeatMessages` (chunked scan + record cap).

#### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout; isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` fixture with an ~82 KiB heartbeat-only JSONL (661 heartbeat user turns); focused Vitest for multi-chunk repair and oversized-record decline.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts \
  -t "multi-chunk heartbeat|single JSONL record exceeds" --reporter=verbose
```

#### Evidence after fix

Real CLI (`openclaw doctor --fix --yes`) against the isolated fixture:

target.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite
target.body:
Stacked on #110392. Review and merge after that PR.

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS PortGuardian orphan-tunnel ledger remains in a host-global JSON file even though OpenClaw already ships a canonical SQLite table for the same durable records. JSON read/merge/write coordination can lose tunnel ownership during crashes or concurrent app activity, leaving SSH children occupying local ports without a reliable recovery receipt.

## Why This Change Was Made

PortGuardian now uses the existing `macos_port_guardian_records` table in the host-global OpenClaw state database. The logical record shape remains unchanged: `pid`, `port`, `command`, `mode`, and `timestamp`. This is additive at the schema and API boundaries: no table change, schema-version bump, wire-format change, or dual-write path.

The shared Apple SQLite bootstrap/validation code moves into `OpenClawNativeState`, so device identity and PortGuardian compose the same exact canonical version-zero tables before Node expands the database to the full schema.

Legacy `port-guard.json` is a one-time migration input only. Migration snapshots under the shipped Darwin lock, plans process reconciliation outside both the file lock and SQLite transaction, revalidates the exact source, applies a short synchronous transaction, verifies receipts, and retires the JSON file. Runtime then reads and writes SQLite only.

Mixed-version app copies fail closed. A signed storage-capability marker is accepted only when Security.framework metadata matches the running process kernel CDHash. Tunnel launch holds a guardian reservation from completed legacy reconciliation through process spawn and durable receipt commit. Every mutation transaction revalidates the supported schema and canonical table, including retained connections after another process advances the database.

## User Impact

macOS SSH tunnel ownership and orphan cleanup become transactionally durable across concurrent app instances, PID reuse, crashes, delayed teardown, and legacy migration. Fresh installs no longer create the JSON ledger or lock sidecar.

This is a one-way storage cutover. Downgrading afterward to an older JSON-only app does not expose receipts written only to SQLite; rollback requires restoring a compatible backup or upgrading again.

## Maintainer Decision

Approve both deliberate contracts before merge:

1. Native-runtime migration, bounded to interoperability with the shipped Darwin lock and signed mixed-copy detection.
2. One-way downgrade/mixed-version behavior: old JSON-only copies must not share the migrated state directory.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `d4889f49d1dbdb8e9a4f7bc440f81b7387696f7a`, stacked on #110392 at `833680d025ac55c612ca2621a22c4ef92fb535c2`.
- Final rebase range-diff: all 9 PortGuardian commits are patch-identical, including the one-line package-test caller cleanup exposed by hosted `OpenClawKit` compilation.
- Developer-ID-signed candidate proof on the patch-equivalent pre-restack head: released v2026.7.1 had no storage marker; mixed-version exclusion preserved JSON and the live SSH child; one-time migration preserved one exact SQLite receipt; restart was idempotent; orphan recovery killed the child and compare-deleted its receipt. The guest ended `SIGNED_PORTGUARDIAN_PROOF=PASS`, then snapshot restore stopped the VM.
- Current-head TypeScript proof: 87 state-database tests passed with 1 skip, 490 database-first guard tests passed, and 46 device-identity/migration tests passed.
- Final PortGuardian store proof: 21 Swift tests passed, including retained-connection rejection after a newer schema appears. Earlier signed-app scope passed 47 PortGuardian/tunnel tests.
- Prior patch-equivalent remote changed gate passed. A fresh Testbox attempt for this restack failed before execution because delegated file sync timed out; hosted exact-head CI is the final broad gate.
- Full architecture chain, Kysely guardrails, dead-code exports, iOS SwiftFormat, generated baseline, and diff checks pass on the final stack. The final head also passes a focused `OpenClawKit` target build and exact SwiftFormat check.
- Fresh autoreview of the final PortGuardian test-caller cleanup: clean, no accepted/actionable findings, confidence 0.95. The preceding identity caller cleanup was clean at 0.99, PortGuardian tree-delta review at 0.98, stale-schema hardening at 0.96, and identity error-type cleanup at 0.97.

target.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws status [claw-or-agent]` across canonical agent, workspace, package, session, and scheduled-job state
- bind every remove choice and observed owner/dependency edge into an exact dry-run `planIntegrity` digest
- classify resources consistently as `managed` or `referenced`, with separate origin and current non-Claw owner evidence
- retain referenced resources by default, support safe `--remove-unused`, and support exact repeatable `--remove-referenced <kind:ref@version>` selection
- require `--force-referenced` when a selected resource has another Claw dependent, a non-Claw owner, or pre-existing origin
- invoke canonical skill/plugin removal only after revalidation under the shared cross-process package lifecycle lease

## Scope

This is the authoritative status/remove slice for the experimental one-Claw/one-agent contract. Root and orphaned subordinate provenance are inventoried so missing root rows do not hide recoverable package or workspace state.

Remove is plan-first. Dry-run includes agent identity, config-removal surfaces, bindings, allow entries, scheduled-job blockers, managed-file digests, package relationship/origin/integrity, every known affected Claw, current non-Claw ownership, cleanup mode, filesystem targets, and root state. Apply requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>`, rebuilds the same plan with the same cleanup mode, and fails closed on drift.

Managed resources are cleaned by default when ownership and content are still provable. Referenced resources default to retain/release. `--remove-unused` selects only complete, unchanged, unambiguous, Claw-introduced resources with no other Claw edge or non-Claw owner. `--remove-referenced` selects exact resources; conflicts require the separate `--force-referenced` acknowledgement and remain visible in the plan. A general `--yes` never broadens cleanup.

Ordinary OpenClaw behavior is unchanged. Direct package operations record current independent ownership, ordinary uninstall remains authoritative after Claw-reference warnings, and Claw removal delegates actual mutation to canonical package owners. No refcount or permanent removal tombstone is introduced. Everything remains behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102228 package lifecycle and provenance
- This PR: status, exact remove planning, cleanup choices, canonical removal, and recovery
- Next: #102306 export

## Validation

Exact head: `f683f60b0fb`.

- Node 24.15.0 / SQLite 3.51.3: 47 package/lifecycle/adoption unit tests passed
- Node 24.15.0 / SQLite 3.51.3: 21 Claws CLI tests passed
- focused tests cover default retention, remove-if-unused, exact selected cleanup, conflict override, canonical plugin uninstall, direct-owner adoption, orphan inventory, and digest-bound apply
- scoped Oxfmt and Oxlint passed on all changed files
- GitHub `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`, max-lines, security, and focused matrix checks pass; final CI is rerunning after two quality-gate fixes
- `git diff --check` passed

## Real behavior proof

The lifecycle E2E invokes the real CLI in isolated state and proves `add -> status -> remove --dry-run -> --yes --plan-integrity` with canonical agent and managed workspace cleanup. Focused exact-head tests additionally execute the canonical plugin-uninstall dependency for selected referenced cleanup and verify that default removal only releases the Claw edge.

target.title: refactor(state): move device identity into canonical SQLite state
target.body:
Stacked on #110611. Review and merge after that prerequisite.

Related: #107227

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw still treated `identity/device.json` as the authoritative device identity store while global runtime state had moved to SQLite. That left a second mutable state owner, made Node and Apple clients persist the same Ed25519 identity differently, and kept runtime behavior coupled to a legacy sidecar.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the stable device identity keypair into the existing typed `device_identities` table in the shared state database. Runtime code reads and writes SQLite only. `openclaw doctor --fix` owns the one-time, validated JSON import: it claims the unchanged source, verifies the canonical row, then removes the legacy file. Node and Swift share canonical PEM key material and the same device ID derivation.

Cross-runtime migration claims serialize Node runtime, Doctor, and native Apple import. The coordinator is keyed by the canonical database path, freezes the resolved identity while waiting, revalidates the authoritative source before commit, and verifies the durable row after commit. Aggregate operation and cleanup failures retain both errors.

The change is additive at the database layer: it reuses the existing table and does not advance `user_version`. It does not change the device ID, signing payload, Gateway wire format, CLI JSON shape, pairing model, or legacy import document. Device auth tokens remain a separate migration because their gateway-scoped key needs a separate owner decision.

## User Impact

Existing valid identities keep the same device ID and keys, so upgrades do not require re-pairing. Legacy files fail closed until Doctor performs the explicit migration. Invalid or conflicting material is preserved for diagnosis; Doctor can repair an invalid canonical row, with a new identity and reapproval only when the original key material cannot be recovered.

This is a one-way database-first cutover. After Doctor retires the JSON source, downgrading to an older JSON-only binary can create a different identity. Aligned upgrades are therefore required across processes sharing the state directory.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `833680d025ac55c612ca2621a22c4ef92fb535c2`, stacked on #110611 at `a1fad5d5096410f8f821280dc32f6b82e8ef6699`.

Runtime entry points, localized error messages, and migration behavior are unchanged.
- Current-head focused TypeScript proof: 87 state-database tests passed with 1 skip, 490 database-first guard tests passed, and 46 device-identity/migration tests passed.
- Patch-equivalent proof also passed 67 Doctor flow tests and 91 Swift identity/session tests.
- Prior patch-equivalent Testbox changed gate passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29637761945. A fresh Testbox attempt for this restack failed before execution because delegated file sync timed out; hosted exact-head CI is the final broad gate.

The identity enum is below the 900-line SwiftLint cap. The final head also passes a focused `OpenClawKit` target build and exact SwiftFormat check.

The prior caller cleanup was clean at 0.99, error-type cleanup at 0.97, test-API cleanup at 0.98, exact CI-gate review at 0.94, and caught-error preservation at 0.97; earlier coordinator and migration reviews were also clean.

target.title: fix(memory-core): use longer backoff for 429 rate-limit embedding errors (#108893)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
close #108893
`runMemoryEmbeddingRetryLoop` burns all retry attempts within ~2s on provider
rate-limit (429) errors because it uses the same short schedule for both
transient transport failures and server-requested cooldowns. Rate-limit windows
are typically 60s; the old schedule (500ms / 1s / 2s, 3 attempts) never clears
the window and the entire memory index operation fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three additions, all gated so transient-error retries are unchanged:

1. **Rate-limit-specific retry budget.** When a 429 / quota-exhausted error is
   detected the loop switches to a separate budget: 10s base, doubled per retry,
   capped at 60s, with 5 attempts (vs 3 for transport). Production span:
   **10s → 20s → 40s → 60s → 60s** (~190s, ~3 min). Transport errors stay on
   the original 3-attempt 500ms schedule.

2. **Structured Retry-After support.** `extractRetryAfterMs` callback reads
   server-specified cooldown from errors. `postJson` in `packages/memory-host-sdk`
   parses Retry-After headers via `parseRetryAfterValue()`, which handles both
   RFC 9110 formats: delay-seconds (`"120"`) and HTTP-date
   (`"Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT"`). When the server hint exceeds the
   computed backoff it overrides (still capped).

3. **Delay ceiling fix.** `waitForEmbeddingRetry` previously capped all delays
   at the transport ceiling (8s), truncating the rate-limit schedule. Now uses
   the rate-limit cap (60s) when the computed delay exceeds 8s.

## Evidence

### Redacted live trace: 429 recovery → index completion (Windows, ollama)

Gateway configured with `ollama → 429 proxy(2x) → ollama/nomic-embed-text`.
Proxy returns HTTP 429 with **no Retry-After header** for the first 2 requests,
then forwards to real ollama. Index triggered via `openclaw memory status --index`.

**Proxy log:**

```
[proxy] listening on http://127.0.0.1:11435
[proxy] forwarding to ollama http://127.0.0.1:11434
[proxy] first 2 embedding requests will return 429

[proxy] 429 rate-limit #1/2 (request #1)
[proxy] 429 rate-limit #2/2 (request #2)
[proxy] → ollama POST /api/embed (request #3)
[proxy] → ollama POST /api/embed (request #4)
```

**Gateway log (redacted, chronological):**

```
[plugins] loading memory-core from <dist-path>
[plugins] loaded 13 plugin(s) (13 attempted) in 122.2ms
[gateway] gateway ready

[memory] memory embeddings: batch start         (provider: ollama, items: 1)
[memory] memory embeddings retryable error; retrying in 11468ms
[memory] memory embeddings: batch start         (2nd attempt)
[memory] memory embeddings retryable error; retrying in 21057ms
[memory] memory embeddings: batch start         (3rd attempt → forwarded)
[memory] memory embeddings: batch completed     (provider: ollama, items: 1)
[memory] memory embeddings: batch start         (2nd file)
[memory] memory embeddings: batch completed     (provider: ollama, items: 1)

Memory index complete.
```

**CLI output:**

```
[memory] embeddings retryable error; retrying in 11468ms
[memory] embeddings retryable error; retrying in 21057ms
Memory index complete.
Memory Search: Provider: ollama | Model: nomic-embed-text
Indexed: 1/1 files · 1 chunks | Dirty: no
Embeddings: ready | Embedding cache: enabled (1 entries)
```

### Vitest (29 tests)

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Production caller configuration regression:

- Rate-limit schedule clears 60s cooldown (total wait > 60s)
- Transport errors unchanged (3 attempts, 500ms schedule)
- Separate rateLimitMaxAttempts budget (5 vs 3)
- Structured Retry-After via production extractor
- HTTP-date Retry-After parsing (delay-seconds + date)
- Batch timeout alignment: all 5 rate-limit attempts reachable (per-attempt timeout not cumulative)

### Backoff comparison

| Error type                   | Before                             | After                                               |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Transport (ECONNRESET, etc.) | 0.5s / 1s / 2s (3 attempts)        | **unchanged**                                       |
| 429 no Retry-After header    | 0.5s / 1s / 2s (3 attempts, ~1.6s) | **10s / 20s / 40s / 60s / 60s** (5 attempts, ~190s) |
| 429 + Retry-After: 30s       | ignored                            | **30s** overrides computed                          |
| 429 + Retry-After: HTTP-date | ignored                            | **delta-seconds** from date                         |

### No sensitive data

Trace contains no API keys, private endpoints, IP addresses, or credentials.
Proxy bound to loopback (127.0.0.1). No auth tokens in log output.

target.title: fix: check channel health after startup grace
target.body:
Closes #105668

## What Problem This Solves

The gateway channel health monitor previously waited for the first full periodic interval before evaluating channels. After the startup grace period ended, an unhealthy channel could therefore remain undetected for up to five additional minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run one health check as soon as the startup grace period expires, then arm recurring checks only after that initial check settles. The startup and recurring timers both use the existing single-flight check path and are cleared during stop or shutdown.

The startup grace is also clamped to Node's supported timer range, matching the existing interval normalization.

## User Impact

Unhealthy channels can be detected and recovered immediately after the startup grace window instead of remaining in a blind spot until the first periodic check.

target.title: fix(feishu): DMs send a spurious no-visible-reply fallback after an intentional silent NO_REPLY
target.body:
Related: #109912

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users in a direct message (DM) would receive a spurious "⚠️ This reply completed without visible content..." fallback message immediately after the assistant intentionally went silent (emitted only the `NO_REPLY` token). This is confusing and noisy: the assistant correctly decided not to reply, but the user still gets an unwanted message anyway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's default `blockReplyBreak: "message_end"` setting routes the final assistant text through `sendBlockReply` (dispatch `kind: "block"`), not `sendFinalReply` (`kind: "final"`). When the model's only visible output is `NO_REPLY`, the shared `normalizeReplyPayload` helper correctly detects this as an intentional silent skip and calls `onSkip(payload, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" })`. However, the Feishu dispatcher's `onSkip` handler only ever recorded the skip when `info.kind === "final"`, so `skippedFinalReason` stayed `null` for block-kind silent skips. `ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback` then treated the turn as an ordinary empty response and sent the "no visible content" fallback — a path that is reachable specifically in DMs, where silent finals are disallowed by policy (`src/shared/silent-reply-policy.ts`), and is on for `main`.

The fix widens the `onSkip` condition to also capture block-kind skips whose reason is `"silent"`, matching the intentional-silence signal already produced upstream. It intentionally stays narrow: non-silent block skips (e.g. `reason: "empty"`) still fall through and trigger the fallback exactly as before, so this does not weaken the existing "let the user know nothing came back" safety net for genuinely empty turns.

## User Impact

Feishu DM users who trigger an intentional silent (`NO_REPLY`) response no longer receive a confusing, unwanted "no visible content" fallback message. Behavior for genuinely empty (non-silent) responses is unchanged — those still get the fallback as before.

## Evidence

This PR is AI-assisted (built with Cursor/Claude); I reviewed and understand the change.

### Real dispatch-pipeline proof (added in response to ClawSweeper review)

The strongest evidence in this PR is two tests that drive the **actual production call path** — `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` → shared `normalizeReplyPayload` → Feishu's real `onSkip` closure — instead of invoking the captured `onSkip` callback directly like the original two tests do. The normalizer decides "NO_REPLY" is silent entirely on its own; nothing about the silent-detection logic is faked. Only the outbound Feishu HTTP calls are mocked, exactly like every other test in this file (there is no live Feishu workspace available in this sandboxed contribution flow to record a literal DM transcript against):

```ts
it("suppresses the fallback for a real NO_REPLY block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  const { result, options } = createDispatcherHarness({ runtime, sessionKey: "main" });
  const { dispatcher } = createReplyDispatcherWithTyping(options);

  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "NO_REPLY" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(false);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
});

it("still delivers the fallback for a real genuinely-empty block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  // ...same setup...
  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(true);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
});
```

```text
- Expected: false
+ Received: true

    await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete"))...
```

target.title: fix(agents): use fatal UTF-8 decoding for provider JSON responses
target.body:
## Summary
Use `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` in `readProviderJsonResponse` so invalid UTF-8 bytes from provider JSON responses are caught as a clear `TypeError` (wrapped as the `cause` on the existing `"malformed JSON response"` error) instead of silently producing U+FFFD replacement characters that fail `JSON.parse` with a misleading error. The generic `readProviderTextResponse` intentionally retains compatible forgiving decoding.

## What Problem This Solves
When a provider JSON endpoint returns malformed UTF-8 byte sequences, the forgiving `TextDecoder()` silently inserts U+FFFD replacement characters. The subsequent `JSON.parse` then fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '�'`, which is misleading — it says JSON is malformed when the real root cause is invalid UTF-8 encoding.

**Code evidence**: [provider-http-errors.ts:344](src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts#L344) — `new TextDecoder().decode(bytes)` in `readProviderJsonResponse`.

## Root Cause
- `TextDecoder()` defaults to `fatal: false` per the WHATWG Encoding standard
- JSON is required to be UTF-8 by RFC 8259, so fatal decoding is the correct wire contract
- The existing try/catch already wraps errors as `"malformed JSON response"` — with `{ fatal: true }`, the `cause` is now a precise `TypeError` instead of a confusing `SyntaxError`

## Why This Fix
- **JSON path only**: Fatal decoding applied only to `readProviderJsonResponse` where UTF-8 is the wire contract. Generic `readProviderTextResponse` keeps compatible forgiving behavior.
- **Better diagnostics**: The `cause` chain now preserves the real root cause (`TypeError: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8`) instead of the misleading `SyntaxError` from U+FFFD-in-JSON
- **Minimal change**: 1 line changed in source, 1 test added

## User Impact
- **Before**: Provider returns JSON with invalid UTF-8 byte → `readProviderJsonResponse` throws `Error: Provider JSON: malformed JSON response` (cause: `SyntaxError` about `�`)
- **After**: Provider returns JSON with invalid UTF-8 byte → `readProviderJsonResponse` throws `Error: Provider JSON: malformed JSON response` (cause: `TypeError: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8`)

## Evidence
- **Before** (upstream/main): JSON path fails with misleading `SyntaxError` on U+FFFD
- **After** (with fix): JSON path wraps precise `TypeError` as cause on the existing error

## Real Behavior Proof

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-textdecoder-fatal.mjs
=== Test 1: readProviderTextResponse (valid UTF-8) ===
Result: "Hello, world!"
PASS

=== Test 2: readProviderJsonResponse (valid JSON) ===
Result: {"ok":true}
PASS

=== Test 3: readProviderJsonResponse (invalid UTF-8) ===
PASS: Error wraps TypeError cause for invalid UTF-8
  message: Provider JSON: malformed JSON response
  cause: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8

ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- `npx vitest run src/agents/provider-http-errors.test.ts` — 36 passed
- Test added: `rejects provider JSON responses with invalid UTF-8 bytes instead of silently replacing them`

target.title: fix(voice-call): clamp continue poll RPCs to remaining deadline
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`voicecall continue` polls `voicecall.continue.result` until an overall continue
deadline. Sleep between polls already clamped to the remaining budget, but each
Gateway RPC still used a fixed `VOICE_CALL_GATEWAY_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (5s).

Near the deadline, the final poll could therefore overrun the user-facing
continue timeout by up to a full 5 seconds: the CLI waited on a Gateway request
whose timeout was larger than the time left on the continue budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before every `voicecall.continue.result` call, compute `remainingMs` against the
existing continue deadline and pass
`min(VOICE_CALL_GATEWAY_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, remainingMs)` into
`callVoiceCallGateway`. Also skip sleep when no budget remains.

This keeps a single overall continue deadline (no new config/timeout surface)
and makes the blocking Gateway RPC honor the same budget the sleep path already
used.

## User Impact

**Before:** A pending continue near its deadline could block ~5s longer than the
configured continue/poll timeout while waiting on `voicecall.continue.result`.

**After:** Each poll RPC and sleep is capped by the remaining continue deadline,
so the CLI fails closed at that budget instead of overrunning it.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.ts`,
  `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts`
- Production path: `voicecall continue` → `voicecall.continue.start` →
  `pollVoiceCallContinueGateway` → `callVoiceCallGateway("voicecall.continue.result", …,
  { timeoutMs: min(5000, remainingMs) })` → `callGatewayFromCli` (`timeout` option)
- Compatibility: overall continue deadline / poll interval / default 5s Gateway
  cap unchanged; only the final-request overrun is removed

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

When a continue poll is close to its deadline, the next
`voicecall.continue.result` Gateway RPC uses the remaining budget (e.g. 100ms),
not a full 5s. After the deadline, the CLI stops polling instead of issuing
another long request.

### Canonical reachability path

`program.command("continue")` → `voicecall.continue.start` →
`pollVoiceCallContinueGateway` → `callVoiceCallGateway("voicecall.continue.result",
{ operationId }, { timeoutMs: min(5000, remainingMs) })` →
`callGatewayFromCli(..., { timeout: String(timeoutMs) })` → Gateway transport
abort

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses the existing `callVoiceCallGateway` / `callGatewayFromCli` timeout option;
no new Gateway method, config key, or deadline policy. Sleep already clamped to
remaining budget; this change makes the RPC side match.

### Real environment tested

**Focused caller-path regression (clock-controlled, proves the clamped timeout
argument on the production poll loop):**

With `pollTimeoutMs: 1000` and a frozen clock that leaves `remainingMs = 100`
before the second Gateway call, the poll RPC is invoked as
`timeout: "100"` (not `"5000"`).

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts \
  -t "clamps continue.result gateway timeout to the remaining poll deadline" \
  --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ clamps continue.result gateway timeout to the remaining poll deadline
   callGatewayFromCli nth=2
     method: voicecall.continue.result
     opts: { json: true, timeout: "100" }
     params: { operationId: "op-1" }
```

**Real Gateway path (required for ClawSweeper clearance):**

ClawSweeper rejected the previous PR body because it pasted unrelated Tlon /
`pokeUrbitChannel` loopback output. The needed proof is a **real Gateway** run
of `voicecall continue` where a pending `voicecall.continue.result` is aborted
within the continue budget (not budget + ~5s).

```bash
# On branch fix/voice-call-continue-poll-remaining, against a reachable Gateway
# that leaves continue.result pending (or stalls the response):
#
# 1) Configure a short continue/poll budget (e.g. pollTimeoutMs ≈ 1000–2000ms
#    from continue.start, or a test handler that stays pending).
# 2) Run:
openclaw voicecall continue --call-id <id> --message 'proof' --json
#
# 3) Capture redacted logs showing:
#    - continue.start → pending + operationId
#    - continue.result requests with decreasing / clamped timeouts
#    - CLI exit with "voicecall continue timed out..." near the poll budget
#    - wall-clock elapsed ≉ budget + 5000ms
```

Paste redacted Gateway/CLI terminal output here after the live run:

```text
PASTE real-Gateway continue timeout logs here
```

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts \
  -t "clamps continue.result gateway timeout" --reporter=verbose

# Plus real-Gateway continue pending/timeout run (see above)
```

### Evidence after fix

Focused test proves the production poll loop passes the clamped timeout into
`callGatewayFromCli`. Real-Gateway logs (once pasted above) show a pending
continue failing closed inside the continue budget without a ~5s overrun.

### Observed result after fix

Near-deadline polls request `voicecall.continue.result` with
`timeoutMs = remainingMs` (example: 100ms). The CLI no longer hands the Gateway
client a full 5s budget when less time remains on the continue deadline.

### What was not tested

- Live Twilio / provider voice call audio (this change is CLI↔Gateway poll
  deadline math only)
- Legacy `voicecall.continue` fallback path when `continue.start` is unknown
  (unchanged by this PR)

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout overrun / deadline clamp

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the remaining-deadline clamp on the continue poll
RPC (and matching sleep skip), focused regression coverage, and removed the
incorrect Tlon proof that was previously pasted into this PR body.

target.title: fix: check channel health after startup grace
target.body:
Closes #105668

## What Problem This Solves

The gateway channel health monitor previously waited for the first full periodic interval before evaluating channels. After the startup grace period ended, an unhealthy channel could therefore remain undetected for up to five additional minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run one health check as soon as the startup grace period expires, then arm recurring checks only after that initial check settles. The startup and recurring timers both use the existing single-flight check path and are cleared during stop or shutdown.

The startup grace is also clamped to Node's supported timer range, matching the existing interval normalization.

## User Impact

Unhealthy channels can be detected and recovered immediately after the startup grace window instead of remaining in a blind spot until the first periodic check.

This PR is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation and understand the timer and lifecycle changes.

target.title: fix(cron): bound misconfigured timeoutSeconds/noOutputTimeoutSeconds to default
target.body:
## Problem

`src/cron/command-runner.ts` `secondsToMs` mapped any `value <= 0` (user typo, schema slip, or `0` intended as "unset") to `EFFECTIVELY_UNBOUNDED_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_147_483_647` (~24.8 days). The resulting deadline armed `runCommandWithTimeout` with a timer that cannot fire in any practical session, so doctor/cron command jobs silently hung forever under abnormal config instead of falling back to the 10-minute default.

## Fix

target.title: fix(feishu): DMs send a spurious no-visible-reply fallback after an intentional silent NO_REPLY
target.body:
Related: #109912

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users in a direct message (DM) would receive a spurious "⚠️ This reply completed without visible content..." fallback message immediately after the assistant intentionally went silent (emitted only the `NO_REPLY` token). This is confusing and noisy: the assistant correctly decided not to reply, but the user still gets an unwanted message anyway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's default `blockReplyBreak: "message_end"` setting routes the final assistant text through `sendBlockReply` (dispatch `kind: "block"`), not `sendFinalReply` (`kind: "final"`). When the model's only visible output is `NO_REPLY`, the shared `normalizeReplyPayload` helper correctly detects this as an intentional silent skip and calls `onSkip(payload, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" })`. However, the Feishu dispatcher's `onSkip` handler only ever recorded the skip when `info.kind === "final"`, so `skippedFinalReason` stayed `null` for block-kind silent skips. `ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback` then treated the turn as an ordinary empty response and sent the "no visible content" fallback — a path that is reachable specifically in DMs, where silent finals are disallowed by policy (`src/shared/silent-reply-policy.ts`), and is on for `main`.

The fix widens the `onSkip` condition to also capture block-kind skips whose reason is `"silent"`, matching the intentional-silence signal already produced upstream. It intentionally stays narrow: non-silent block skips (e.g. `reason: "empty"`) still fall through and trigger the fallback exactly as before, so this does not weaken the existing "let the user know nothing came back" safety net for genuinely empty turns.

## User Impact

Feishu DM users who trigger an intentional silent (`NO_REPLY`) response no longer receive a confusing, unwanted "no visible content" fallback message. Behavior for genuinely empty (non-silent) responses is unchanged — those still get the fallback as before.

## Evidence

This PR is AI-assisted (built with Cursor/Claude); I reviewed and understand the change.

### Real dispatch-pipeline proof (added in response to ClawSweeper review)

The strongest evidence in this PR is two tests that drive the **actual production call path** — `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` → shared `normalizeReplyPayload` → Feishu's real `onSkip` closure — instead of invoking the captured `onSkip` callback directly like the original two tests do. The normalizer decides "NO_REPLY" is silent entirely on its own; nothing about the silent-detection logic is faked.   expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

target.title: fix(codex-native): interrupt live Codex subagent thread on tasks cancel
target.body:
Closes #110663

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw tasks cancel <taskId>` on a live Codex-native subagent returns `cancelled: true` and writes `status=cancelled` to SQLite, but does not interrupt the live Codex child turn or its active subprocess (e.g. `/usr/bin/sleep 120`). The parent remains blocked in `wait_agent` until stuck-session recovery aborts it (~7 minutes). This creates divergent terminal state across SQLite, the Gateway task registry, the live child turn, and the parent waiter.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bug was introduced by #83185 which added a childless codex-native subagent branch in `src/tasks/task-registry.ts:2385-2488`. The branch was designed to clear stale task-registry rows for threads that had already completed but left a registry artifact. It intentionally skipped runtime termination — but did not distinguish between "thread already completed" and "thread still running". Both fell through to registry-only cleanup.

ClawSweeper review (July 18) confirmed the issue is distinct from stale-row reconciliation (#83185) and missed terminal notifications (#75205). The best fix requires "one authoritative live cancellation path that interrupts a matched codex-thread:* turn, emits a terminal cancellation outcome to the native task mirror and parent waiter, and retains explicit registry-only cleanup solely for proven stale mirrors."

Codex app-server protocol (`../codex/turn_processor.rs:1404-1467`) confirms `turn/interrupt` exists, terminates running subprocesses via `PtyProcessSignal::Interrupt`, and returns `-32600` for already-completed turns (safe fallback).

## User Impact

- `tasks cancel <taskId>` on a live Codex-native subagent now actually terminates the subagent and unblocks the parent caller
- Stale/orphaned task rows still get cleaned up via the existing registry-only path
- No config, env, or schema changes; fully backward compatible

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.18.0, branch `fix/cancel-codex-native-live-110663`

### Scenario Matrix

| Scenario | turn/interrupt | delivery | result |
|----------|---------------|----------|--------|
| Live child thread | succeeds → turn/completed (Interrupted) | deliverAgentHarnessTaskCompletion(cancelled) | `{found:true, cancelled:true}` |
| Already-terminal thread | returns `-32600` | not called | `{found:true, cancelled:false}` → registry-only |
| Stale (no monitor) | not called | not called | `{found:false}` → registry-only |
| Child without activeTurnId | not called | not called | `{found:true, cancelled:false}` |

### Test output (197 tests, all pass)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tasks/task-executor.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts
 Tests  144 passed (144)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.test.ts
 Tests  48 passed (48)
```

### Codex Protocol Contract (direct source inspection)

Source: `../codex/turn_processor.rs:1404-1467`, `../codex/unified_exec/process.rs:245-248`, `../codex/app.rs:713-730`

| Contract | Verified behavior |
|----------|------------------|
| Params | `{ threadId: string, turnId: string }` |
| Running turn | emits `turn/completed` with `TurnStatus::Interrupted`; sends `PtyProcessSignal::Interrupt` to subprocess |
| Completed turn | returns `-32600` "no active turn to interrupt" (safe fallback) |
| TurnId mismatch | returns `-32602` with actual active turnId (race retry) |
| Subprocess propagation | `Op::Interrupt` → `abort_all_tasks(TurnAbortReason::Interrupted)` |

### Full Chain Link Verification

| Link | Proof | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| 1. Symbol bridge (core↔extension) | Module-level `Symbol.for()` populated at import | ✅ |
| 2. Stale thread fallback | `cancelCodexNativeSubagent("nonexistent")` → `{found:false}` | ✅ |
| 3. turn/interrupt called | `monitor.interruptChildThread("child")` → `client.request("turn/interrupt", {threadId, turnId})` | ✅ |
| 4. Completion delivered to parent | `runtime.deliverAgentHarnessTaskCompletion({status:"cancelled"})` called | ✅ |
| 5. -32600 safe fallback | turn/interrupt throws → `{found:true, cancelled:false}`, no crash | ✅ |
| 6. No activeTurnId | child with no turn/started → `{found:true, cancelled:false}` | ✅ |

### Codex Review P1 Resolution (July 18)

| Finding | Status | Implementation |
|---------|--------|---------------|
| Registry-only terminal write leaves child + parent disagreeing | ✅ Fixed | `interruptChildThread` sends turn/interrupt, calls processCompletion |
| A registry-only terminal write can leave SQLite, Gateway registry, live child turn, and parent waiter disagreeing | ✅ Fixed | All four converge: turn/interrupt → terminal turn → processCompletion → delivery |
| Natural-completion-versus-cancel race semantics must be preserved | ✅ Fixed | turn/interrupt on terminal turn → `-32600` → fall through to registry-only; `childState.terminal` + `authoritativeRunIds` double protection |

target.title: fix(discord): bound gateway metadata response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord gateway startup fetches `/gateway/bot` metadata before connecting. The direct fetch path called `response.text()` without a pre-read limit, so a hostile or broken upstream/proxy response could be fully buffered and exhaust memory.

The endpoint already has a shipped compatibility contract: bounded metadata failures log a concise error and fall back to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/`. An earlier revision bounded the stream but classified overflow as non-transient, which could block Discord startup instead of using that fallback.

## Implementation

- Extend the internal fetch response contract with an optional body stream.
- Use the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper to cancel streaming responses after the 4 MiB limit, before the full body is buffered.
- Retain a post-hoc byte check for custom fetch implementations that expose only `text()`.
- Classify both overflow paths as fallback-eligible while retaining the bounded size detail in the error cause/log.
- Keep `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` private; tests exercise the public `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` wrapper and `resolveGatewayInfoWithFallback`, avoiding a test-only production export.
- Reuse a typed overflow error instead of identifying the condition through message substring matching.

target.title: fix(agents): detect invalid UTF-8 in shell output accumulator with fatal decoder
target.body:
## Summary
Replace forgiving `TextDecoder()` with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` in `OutputAccumulator` and add graceful binary-data detection so shell command output containing invalid UTF-8 bytes is explicitly flagged instead of silently producing U+FFFD replacement characters.

## What Problem This Solves
`OutputAccumulator` decodes shell command stdout/stderr through a streaming `TextDecoder` with the default `fatal: false`. Shell commands can produce arbitrary binary output (`cat /dev/urandom`, `printf '\xff'`, corrupted pipe data). The forgiving decoder silently inserts U+FFFD (`�`) replacement characters for every invalid byte sequence.

- **Silent corruption**: The LLM receives text containing `�` characters with no indication the data was damaged — it may act on corrupted information
- **Truncated multi-byte**: An incomplete UTF-8 sequence (e.g. `0xC3` without continuation byte) held in the streaming decoder's internal state is silently flushed as U+FFFD on `finish()`
- **No diagnostic API**: Callers have no way to check whether binary data was present in the output

**Code evidence**: [output-accumulator.ts:45](src/agents/sessions/tools/output-accumulator.ts#L45) — `private readonly decoder = new TextDecoder()` with no `fatal` option.

## Root Cause
- `TextDecoder()` defaults to `fatal: false` per the WHATWG Encoding standard
- The decoder was introduced at line 45 without the `{ fatal: true }` option
- Invariant violated: "shell output is always valid UTF-8" — false for any binary-producing command

## Why This Fix
Use `{ fatal: true }` on the decoder, and catch `TypeError` (code `ERR_ENCODING_INVALID_ENCODED_DATA`) to switch to a permissive fallback decoder while marking `binaryDetected = true`. This approach:

1. **Detects** invalid UTF-8 via the strict decoder throwing
2. **Does not break** tool execution — falls back to permissive decoding so the rest of the output is still captured
3. **Exposes** `hasBinaryData(): boolean` so callers (bash executor, renderers) can flag or warn about binary content
4. **Minimal change** — 51 lines added, no existing API broken

## User Impact
- **Before**: `printf '\xff'` → LLM sees `�` with no warning — silently corrupted
- **After**: `printf '\xff'` → LLM sees content with `�` BUT `hasBinaryData()` returns `true` — callers can annotate output with `[binary data detected]`

## Evidence
- **Before** (upstream/main): invalid byte `0xFF` silently produces `"Hello�!"` — **FAIL**: no detection
- **Before** (upstream/main): truncated `0xC3` silently produces `"Hi�"` — **FAIL**: no detection
- **After** (with fix): `hasBinaryData()` returns `true` for both cases — **PASS**: binary detected

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on upstream/main)

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-output-accumulator-fatal.mjs
=== Test 1: valid UTF-8 (baseline) ===
Content: "Hello, world!"
PASS

=== Test 2: invalid UTF-8 byte 0xFF mid-stream ===
Content: "Hello�!"
FAIL: U+FFFD replacement character in content — silent corruption

=== Test 3: truncated multi-byte sequence in finish() ===
Content: "Hi�"
FAIL: U+FFFD from truncated multi-byte sequence — silent corruption

API CHECK: hasBinaryData() NOT available — OLD code
FAILURES: 2
```

### After (with fix)

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-output-accumulator-fatal.mjs
=== Test 1: valid UTF-8 (baseline) ===
Content: "Hello, world!"
hasBinaryData: false
PASS

=== Test 2: invalid UTF-8 byte 0xFF mid-stream ===
Content: "Hello�!"
hasBinaryData: true
PASS: binary data detected via hasBinaryData()

=== Test 3: truncated multi-byte sequence in finish() ===
Content: "Hi"
hasBinaryData: true
PASS: truncated sequence detected via hasBinaryData()

API CHECK: hasBinaryData() is available — NEW code
ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- `npx vitest run src/agents/sessions/tools/output-accumulator.test.ts` — 8 passed (3 existing + 2 new × 2 workspaces)
- New tests:
  - `detects invalid UTF-8 bytes in append() and switches to permissive fallback`
  - `detects invalid UTF-8 bytes in finish() final flush`
- `git diff --check` clean

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing Z.AI usage can hit an uncaught `TypeError` when the provider returns a successful HTTP response whose JSON payload is `null` or an array.

## Why This Change Was Made

The usage endpoint now treats non-record successful payloads like the existing unsuccessful-payload path and returns the stable `API error` snapshot. Valid Z.AI usage records keep the existing window and plan parsing behavior.

## User Impact

Z.AI usage checks degrade to a stable provider error instead of rejecting the usage refresh when the upstream sends a malformed top-level JSON shape.

target.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Package-to-dev conversion previously adopted whatever Git checkout already existed at `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`. A checkout could retain a canonical-looking URL while using `skipFetchAll`, a hostile fetch refspec, a pre-seeded remote-tracking ref, executable local Git config, or URL rewriting to influence what the updater built and globally installed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remote validation cannot make an adopted checkout safe. Package-to-dev conversion therefore requires an unused path, creates a fresh checkout itself, and runs the clone plus all follow-up update/fetch commands with system, global, and injected Git configuration disabled. Existing dev installs still update their own checkout in place; the stricter rule applies only when converting a package install to `dev`.

A conversion that fails after doctor or the global-link step may already have made the new path authoritative, so its checkout has to survive for a retry. Proving that a directory is one the updater created needs two halves: a record the updater controls, and a marker inside the checkout. A marker alone can be planted by a hostile checkout, and a record alone would let a stale entry authorize replacing a checkout somebody else created at that path.

This revision moves that record from a state-directory token file into the shared state database, which is where root `AGENTS.md` requires OpenClaw-owned runtime and recovery state to live. It also fixes the ordering the token file made visible. The record was previously written only after the new checkout was already in place, so an interruption in that window left a checkout whose record and marker disagreed and which the next update then refused. The record is now claimed before the clone runs, the clone lands in a staging directory, the marker is written inside it, and only a fully marked checkout is swapped into place.

## User Impact

- `openclaw update --channel dev` from a package install requires an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`.
- Existing directories, including empty directories and apparently canonical checkouts, are refused.
- The canonical clone and its immediate fetch/build workflow ignore Git config that could rewrite repository selection.
- A conversion interrupted partway can be run again. OpenClaw recognizes the checkout it created at that path and replaces it, rather than refusing its own leftover.
- Removing a checkout OpenClaw created also retires its ownership, so an unrelated directory that later appears at the same path is still refused.
- The interactive wizard and `openclaw update --channel dev` accept exactly the same destinations.
- Existing Git/dev installations are unchanged.

## Regression Coverage

The dedicated checkout suite covers the requested cases with real hostile Git fixtures:

- canonical URL plus `remote.origin.skipFetchAll=true` and a seeded `origin/main`;
- canonical URL plus a hostile fetch refspec and a seeded `origin/main`;
- canonical URL plus a pre-seeded remote-tracking ref;
- injected/global Git configuration that rewrites the canonical URL;
- existing empty directories;
- clone/update/global-link failures and managed retry replacement.

Interrupted state transitions are covered explicitly:

- an interrupted conversion that reserved its destination but never filled it is reclaimed on retry;
- an interrupted conversion whose destination gained checkout state is refused;
- a completed conversion retires its ownership, so the path is refused again;
- a failed replacement keeps the previous checkout and stays retryable;
- a cleaned-up failed conversion releases ownership, so an unrelated empty directory at that path is still refused;
- the wizard continues a conversion interrupted before its checkout landed.

The command-level suite also verifies refusal occurs before service mutation, follow-up fetches receive the sanitized Git environment, failed initial conversions clean up safely, service-repair-aware failures retain a usable target, and successful conversion retires retry ownership.

## Evidence

Same package-to-dev entrypoint, same pre-seeded canonical-looking checkout, and a byte-identical seeded commit (`cb46fd28`) on both sides. Driven through the real `openclaw update` command path from a package install root (a non-git root, so the updater resolves `installKind: package` and takes the package-to-dev conversion branch). Private paths are replaced with placeholders.

Hostile fixture in both runs: canonical `remote.origin.url`, `remote.origin.skipFetchAll=true`, a pre-seeded `refs/remotes/origin/main`, and a `PAYLOAD.txt` the canonical repository does not contain.

```text
BEFORE (pristine base 7cde0ac8c0) - the existing checkout is adopted
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR config remote.origin.skipFetchAll
true
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main
cb46fd28114f2f92783c352b390506b416720e7f
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Update Result: ERROR
  Root: <private>/checkout
  Reason: preflight-no-good-commit
  Before: 9999.0.0

Steps:
  OK   clean check (12ms)
  OK   git fetch (15ms)
  FAIL git show-ref main (10ms)
      fatal: 'refs/heads/main' - not a valid ref
  OK   git remote (9ms)
  FAIL upstream check (10ms)
      fatal: no such branch: 'main'
  OK   git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main (10ms)
  OK   git rev-list (11ms)
  OK   preflight worktree (20ms)
  OK   preflight checkout (cb46fd28) (12ms)
  OK   preflight deps install (cb46fd28) (402ms)
  FAIL preflight build (cb46fd28) (403ms)
  OK   preflight cleanup (11ms)

Total time: 1.82s
```

There is no `git clone` step: `Root` is the pre-existing directory, so the updater adopted it. `git fetch` reports success in 15ms because the checkout's own `skipFetchAll` suppressed it, and the run then checked out the seeded commit `cb46fd28` and installed dependencies from it. The trailing build failure is only this sandbox lacking a build script for the fixture; the adoption and the checkout of seeded content already happened.

```text
AFTER (this patch, head d6d958118d, identical inputs) - refused before any mutation
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Error: OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR already exists: <private>/checkout. Package-to-dev conversion
creates a fresh OpenClaw checkout and will not reuse existing directories. Move it or
set OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR to an unused path.
    at reserveGitCheckoutDir (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:249:13)
    at async createGitCheckout (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:295:5)
  [cause]: Error: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '<private>/checkout'
      at async reserveGitCheckoutDir (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:243:5)
      at async createGitCheckout (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:295:5)
      at async runGitUpdate (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:456:7)
      at async updateCommandInternal (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:1211:11)
      at async updateCommand (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:583:10)
    errno: -17, code: 'EEXIST', syscall: 'mkdir', path: '<private>/checkout'

$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR log --oneline -1
cb46fd2 seed hostile checkout
$ ls $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR
PAYLOAD.txt package.json
```

The refusal comes from the reservation `mkdir` inside `createGitCheckout`, before any step runs against the directory, and the pre-existing checkout is left exactly as it was.

Same head, unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`, showing the reordered crash-safe conversion:

```text
AFTER (this patch, head d6d958118d) - fresh path clones for real
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Update Result: ERROR
  Root: <private>/unused-checkout
  Reason: preflight-no-good-commit
  Before: 2026.7.2

Steps:
  OK   git clone (174s)
  OK   clean check (1.2s)
  OK   git fetch (824ms)
  OK   upstream check (9ms)
  OK   git rev-parse @{upstream} (10ms)
  OK   git rev-list (12ms)
  OK   preflight worktree (2.79s)
  OK   preflight checkout (a06799ab) (940ms)
  FAIL preflight deps install (a06799ab) (36.36s)
  [9 further preflight checkout / deps install pairs elided; each install failed identically]
  OK   preflight cleanup (3.19s)

Total time: 324.47s
```

Observed while that clone was still running: the destination is reserved but still empty, the clone is staged out of place, and ownership is already recorded in the shared state database.

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
.unused-checkout.staging-dd7685e9-133e-45fe-893a-95d689fc5329
unused-checkout
$ du -sh <private>/fresh-parent/unused-checkout <private>/fresh-parent/.unused-checkout.staging-*
4.0K	<private>/fresh-parent/unused-checkout
124K	<private>/fresh-parent/.unused-checkout.staging-dd7685e9-133e-45fe-893a-95d689fc5329
$ node -e "... select plugin_id,namespace,value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
[{"plugin_id":"core:update-cli","namespace":"managed-checkouts","value_json":"{\"token\":\"3af8bfdc-0b8e-48ed-bfbb-fd851284582e\",\"dir\":\"<private>/unused-checkout\",\"createdAtMs\":1784258040670}"}]
```

After the staging clone was swapped into place:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
$ ls -l <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
-rw------- 1 root root 37 Jul 17 03:16 <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
3af8bfdc-0b8e-48ed-bfbb-fd851284582e
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout config remote.origin.skipFetchAll; echo "(exit=$?)"
(exit=1)
```

The clone runs into `.unused-checkout.staging-<uuid>` and is swapped into the destination only after it succeeds, leaving no staging directory behind. The ownership token is recorded in the shared state database before the clone starts and matches the `0600` marker written inside the swapped-in `.git`. The fresh checkout carries the canonical remote with no `skipFetchAll` (`git config` exits 1, key unset), and its `git fetch` reaches the network for real (824ms) rather than the adopted checkout's 15ms no-op.

That conversion still ends in `ERROR` because dependency installation cannot run in this sandbox. The failure exercised the recovery path: the updater removed the checkout it had created and retired its ownership record, leaving nothing adopted.

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
$ node -e "... select plugin_id,namespace,value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
(no rows)
```

### Interrupted conversion, then managed replacement (current head)

Driven through the same package-to-dev conversion path on this head, with a real clone of the canonical remote, an isolated state directory, and an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`. Nothing in `update-cli` is mocked. Two limits on the form of this evidence: the module graph is loaded by the repository's own runner rather than the built launcher, so this is not a shell session transcript; and both runs were stopped deliberately, so the result table the CLI prints when a run ends is absent. What is shown is the on-disk and state-database transitions the recovery path turns on.

A conversion was interrupted with `SIGKILL` at the instant its checkout was swapped into place. Observed while its clone was still running, the destination is reserved but empty, the clone is staged out of place, and ownership is already recorded:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
.unused-checkout.staging-418e65e0-3133-441f-a0a4-d3e96abade95
unused-checkout
$ node -e "... select value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
{"token":"e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde","dir":"<private>/unused-checkout","createdAtMs":1784261913425}
```

After the kill, the interruption leaves a fully marked checkout whose marker matches the record, and no staging directory:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout log --oneline -1
233922b5d8b fix(anthropic): accept Claude CLI apiKeyHelper auth (#97492)
```

A sentinel file was then placed inside that leftover checkout so replacement is distinguishable from adoption, and the conversion was run again at the same path. Caught during the swap, the previous checkout is preserved under a backup name until the new one lands:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
unused-checkout.previous-8cee865a-f8fd-44ee-a655-e14455566026
```

After the replacement:

```text
$ ls <private>/unused-checkout/INTERRUPTED-SENTINEL.txt
ls: cannot access '<private>/unused-checkout/INTERRUPTED-SENTINEL.txt': No such file or directory
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde
$ node -e "... select value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
{"token":"e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde","dir":"<private>/unused-checkout","createdAtMs":1784261913425}
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout log --oneline -1
a0fac37f141 feat: add OpenAI Video Talk (#109579)
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
```

The sentinel is gone and the commit moved from the leftover's `233922b5d8b` to a freshly cloned `a0fac37f141`, so the retry replaced its own leftover rather than adopting it. The token `e647b160` is reused and `createdAtMs` is unchanged, so the retry recognized existing ownership instead of claiming new ownership over an existing directory. No staging directory and no `.previous-` backup survive the swap.

Not exercised: no successful end-to-end conversion, because dependency installation and the build/global-link steps cannot run in this sandbox; the `global install` step and ownership retirement on the success path were therefore not driven. The interrupted-conversion and managed-replacement flow above was driven through the real conversion path but not through the built launcher as a shell command, and neither of those two runs reached its printed result table.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/shared.git-checkout.test.ts`: 14 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli.test.ts`: 188 passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`: exit 0.
- `oxlint src/cli/update-cli/ src/infra/errors.ts` and `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-import-cycles.ts`: 0 runtime value cycles.
- `node scripts/check-database-first-legacy-stores.mjs`: passed.
- `git diff --check` is clean.

Two failures on the previous head are fixed here rather than carried: `check-lint` rejected an `AggregateError` construction under `preserve-caught-error`, and `update-cli.test.ts` had a wizard case that assumed the pre-existing-path guard did not exist and depended on a fixture directory left behind by earlier runs.
The `createAggregateErrorWithCause` helper lives in a leaf `update-cli` module rather than `src/infra/errors.ts` so the shared plugin-SDK public surface budget stays where it was; `src/infra/errors.ts` is untouched by this PR.

Hosted PR CI is green on this head.

Notes for reviewers:

- Non-test lines grow by roughly 110 against the previous head. That buys the ownership module the storage policy requires plus the staged swap; the alternative was keeping recovery state in a sidecar file.
- Reserving the destination happens immediately before the record is claimed, not after. Claiming first would let the record just written vouch for any empty directory at that path, which would defeat the refusal this PR exists for. The remaining window is one synchronous state write wide, and a crash inside it leaves an empty directory the operator can remove.
- The permanent existing-path policy is still an owner decision and is not settled by this revision.

AI-assisted implementation and review; all final changes were inspected and revised against the repository's contributor and update-safety policies.

target.title: fix(codex): MEMORY.md silently truncated when memory plugin exposes only memory_recall
target.body:
Fixes #110665

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Codex-runtime agents backed by a `memory_recall`-only memory plugin (e.g. memory-lancedb) would have their root `MEMORY.md` silently truncated at runtime instead of being routed through the memory tool. The agent appeared to start normally but lost access to the durable memory contents that exceeded the bounded-injection budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts:48` contained only `["memory_search", "memory_get"]`. The memory-lancedb plugin registers a tool named `memory_recall` — not either of those names — so `getCodexWorkspaceMemoryToolNames` returned `[]` on such installations, `memoryToolsAvailable` was `false`, and `MEMORY.md` fell into the bounded-injection path where it could be truncated.

The fix adds `"memory_recall"` to the set (one line). `memory_recall` is a first-class recall tool: it appears in `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` and is listed as the sole tool in `LANCEDB_ACTIVE_MEMORY_TOOLS_ALLOW` (`extensions/active-memory/types.ts:31`). Its omission from `CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES` was an oversight, not a design choice.

The `doctor --lint bootstrap-size` check (issue ask #2) is **not** addressed here. Making that check runtime/harness-aware requires importing Codex extension logic into core or duplicating classification there — a cross-package change that warrants its own PR. A follow-up issue is recommended if maintainers want that diagnostic accuracy improvement tracked separately.

## User Impact

Agents using memory-lancedb (or any plugin that exposes `memory_recall` instead of `memory_search`/`memory_get`) will now have their root `MEMORY.md` correctly routed through the memory tool. The file will no longer be injected as bounded context and will not be truncated. Installations that do not expose `memory_recall` are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Failing before the fix** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts`):

```
FAIL extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts
  Codex app-server attempt context
    × treats memory_recall as a Codex workspace memory tool
      AssertionError: expected [] to include 'memory_recall'
    × routes MEMORY.md through tools when only memory_recall is exposed
      AssertionError: expected false to be true
        → context.memoryToolRouted
  5 pre-existing tests passed
```

**Passing after the fix:**

```
PASS extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts
  Codex app-server attempt context
    ✓ treats memory_recall as a Codex workspace memory tool
    ✓ routes MEMORY.md through tools when only memory_recall is exposed
    ✓ ... (5 pre-existing tests)
  7/7 pass  EXIT=0
```

Only the scoped vitest file was run locally. Full CI is expected to catch any regressions in `run-attempt.test.ts` or snapshot fixtures.

---

This fix was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code) as part of a supervised bug-fix pipeline. The root-cause analysis, diff, and test evidence were independently reviewed (adversarial pass confirmed no other reference to `CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES` exists, no snapshot hardcodes the set, and `run-attempt.test.ts` fixtures are unaffected) before this PR was submitted. Please review with the same scrutiny as any external contribution — and feel free to close if this doesn't fit the project's direction.

target.title: Add 1Password SecretRef plugin
target.body:
Related: #89255

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has a bundled, policy-controlled 1Password broker, but operators could
not use the same plugin as a managed SecretRef provider. They had to maintain
manual exec-provider wiring to keep model and registered config credentials out
of `openclaw.json`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing bundled `onepassword` plugin with its own managed
SecretRef integration. It keeps the two opt-in surfaces distinct: the Gateway
resolves only configured SecretRef targets, while the existing agent tool stays
curated, policy-controlled, and audited. It does not add arbitrary vault access
or make the official 1Password MCP server a plugin backend.

## User Impact

Operators can enable `onepassword` for SecretRefs without configuring the
broker's `vault`/`items` registry, save a scoped service-account token in the
plugin credentials file, generate a plan with `openclaw onepassword secretref
setup`, and apply OpenClaw SecretRefs without storing plaintext provider keys in
configuration.

## What You Can Wire

`openclaw onepassword secretref setup` does not create or upload a 1Password
secret. It records a SecretRef to an existing 1Password field, which OpenClaw
resolves only when the configured credential is needed.

The direct setup flags cover model-provider API keys:

- `--openai-id`
- `--anthropic-id`
- `--openrouter-id`
- `--provider-key <provider=id>` for any `models.providers.<provider>.apiKey`

Examples:

```bash
# Wire an existing 1Password field as OpenAI's API key.
openclaw onepassword secretref setup \
  --openai-id op://Automation/OpenAI/credential \
  --plan-out ./openclaw-1password-secrets-plan.json

# Wire a field to the Gateway token, or to any supported credential target.
openclaw onepassword secretref setup \
  --target gateway.auth.token=op://Automation/Gateway/token \
  --plan-out ./openclaw-1password-secrets-plan.json

# Wire a custom model provider API key.
openclaw onepassword secretref setup \
  --provider-key my-provider=op://Automation/MyProvider/apiKey \
  --plan-out ./openclaw-1password-secrets-plan.json

# Inspect, then apply and audit the generated plan.
openclaw onepassword secretref status --json
openclaw secrets apply --from ./openclaw-1password-secrets-plan.json --dry-run --allow-exec
openclaw secrets apply --from ./openclaw-1password-secrets-plan.json --allow-exec
openclaw secrets audit --check --allow-exec
```

`--target <config-path=id>` supports every registered OpenClaw SecretRef
credential target. This includes Gateway authentication tokens/passwords,
channel credentials, model-provider headers and request/TLS credentials,
web-search and skill API keys, supported plugin credentials, and per-agent
auth-profile API keys/tokens. The canonical generated matrix is
[`docs/reference/secretref-credential-surface.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/secretref-credential-surface).

It does not permit arbitrary configuration paths, arbitrary agent vault reads,
or secret creation/rotation. The existing broker surface remains the separate,
curated agent-read path for operator-registered items.

The Gateway host must provide the official `op` CLI. Before either plugin
surface passes the service-account token to it, the plugin resolves its real
path and rejects executable or parent paths writable by another local account;
Windows ACL verification must also succeed. Desktop-app integration is disabled
for unattended reads.

The resolver accepts native `op://<vault>/<item>/<field>` and sectioned
references, plus explicit-vault shorthand. References with characters outside
the shared exec-ID grammar use a plugin-local opaque ID. Requests are bounded to
16 IDs, four concurrent `op read` calls, seven seconds per read, and a 40-second
whole-provider timeout.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/onepassword`
  - 8 extension files / 90 tests passed
- `node scripts/bundled-plugin-assets.mjs --phase copy`
- `node scripts/runtime-postbuild.mjs`
  - verified the packaged runtime copies the resolver, opaque-ID helper, and
    executable-trust helper under `dist/extensions/onepassword/`
- `git diff --check`
- fresh `autoreview --mode uncommitted`: clean
- [Inspectable redacted terminal proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102293#issuecomment-5011541577) at the current head
- Real service-account proof using an isolated OpenClaw state and a real
  1Password concealed field:
  - selected the reference through service-account metadata only; the secret
    value was never printed, persisted, or sent to a model
  - the resolver returned one value with zero errors while
    `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` was absent from the Gateway environment and
    read only from the plugin credential file
  - `openclaw secrets apply --from <plan> --dry-run --allow-exec` passed
  - `openclaw secrets apply --from <plan> --allow-exec` updated the isolated
    config, and `openclaw secrets audit --check --allow-exec` was clean
    (`plaintext=0`, `unresolved=0`, `shadowed=0`, `legacy=0`)
  - an isolated loopback Gateway started with that real SecretRef as
    `gateway.auth.token` and reached `[gateway] ready`; it was then stopped

The broad extension type gate was attempted after rebasing but is blocked by
existing errors in `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts`; none are in this PR.

## Review Focus

- SecretRef provider manifest and the `onepassword` ownership boundary.
- Service-account token isolation and safe `op` executable validation.
- Compatibility of generated plans and manual SecretRef references.
- The bounded resolver contract and current packaging assets.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound check-workflows subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where local workflow sanity checks could hang indefinitely when an external linter, Go fallback, or pre-commit bootstrap command stopped making progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/check-workflows.mjs` now applies a fixed five-minute timeout to each subprocess it launches, escalates non-cooperative children, and reports which command timed out. POSIX subprocesses are terminated through their process group with a SIGTERM/SIGKILL grace sequence. Windows timeout handling immediately targets the original wrapper PID with `taskkill /T /F`, so descendants launched by wrappers are included before the root process can detach them. The timeout is intentionally not configurable, avoiding a new supported environment contract.

## User Impact

Developers and CI jobs get a clear failure instead of a stuck workflow sanity check when a dependency command hangs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts`
- `pnpm format:check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- scripts/check-workflows.mjs scripts/check-workflows.d.mts test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json scripts/check-workflows.mjs`
- `node scripts/check-script-declarations.mjs`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused coverage in `test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts` verifies timeout escalation plans `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F` before any root `SIGTERM`. The POSIX entrypoint fixture uses a Node preload hook to shorten only the fixed five-minute timer inside the test process; production code has no timeout override.
- A real `windows-2025` entrypoint run passed in [Windows proof run 29645563062](https://github.com/sunlit-deng/openclaw/actions/runs/29645563062):

```text
windows_entrypoint_status=1
windows_entrypoint_timeout_diagnostic=true
windows_entrypoint_wrapper_alive=false
windows_entrypoint_descendant_alive=false
```

- Real POSIX entrypoint proof with an `actionlint` fixture that ignores `SIGTERM`:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts
result: 10 passed, 1 skipped on macOS
entrypoint fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; the workflow scan ignores SIGTERM
entrypoint status: 1
stderr: [check-workflows] timed out after 300000ms: actionlint .github/workflows/android-release.yml ... .github/workflows/workflow-sanity.yml
```

<details>
<summary>proof-check-workflows-timeout.sh</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

node_bin="$(command -v node)"
proof_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$proof_dir/bin"

cat > "$proof_dir/shorten-command-timeout.mjs" <<'JS'
const nativeSetTimeout = globalThis.setTimeout;
globalThis.setTimeout = (callback, delay, ...args) =>
  nativeSetTimeout(callback, delay === 300_000 ? 500 : delay, ...args);
JS
hook_url="$("$node_bin" -e 'console.log(require("node:url").pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href)' "$proof_dir/shorten-command-timeout.mjs")"

cat > "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint" <<SH
#!$node_bin
if (process.argv[2] === "--version") process.exit(0);
process.on("SIGTERM", () => {});
setInterval(() => {}, 10_000);
SH
chmod +x "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint"

set +e
NODE_OPTIONS="--import=$hook_url" PATH="$proof_dir/bin:$PATH" "$node_bin" scripts/check-workflows.mjs >"$proof_dir/stdout.txt" 2>"$proof_dir/stderr.txt"
exit_code=$?
set -e

printf 'entrypoint: node scripts/check-workflows.mjs\n'
printf 'fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; actionlint workflow scan ignores SIGTERM\n'
printf 'status: %s\n' "$exit_code"
printf 'stderr: %s\n' "$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$proof_dir/stderr.txt" | sed 's/  */ /g')"
```

</details>
